title: Annotatio VI §.I open: Indignorum — prelibate sacramental-eating term before Indigni
pass_a_gloss: ANNOTATION VI. On the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body by the Unworthy. §. I. Although we more fully examined the term and reason of Oral Eating of Christ’s body in the preceding Annotation; yet, since on one side Lutheran theologians of clearer judgment begin to nauseate at this term as also to be predicated of the Unworthy, and predicated, a term of Sacramental Eating being substituted in its place; and on the other side the Reformed hardly deny that a certain Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body can fall even on the unworthy — something must be tasted here of this term Sacramental Eating, before we determine anything either about the Unworthy to whom that Eating is attributed, or about the Truth and Necessity of this Attribution.
pass_b_english: Annotatio VI opens on Oral eating of Christ’s body by the unworthy. §.I first pauses the term itself.

Clearer Lutheran judges are sick of predicating “Oral” of the unworthy and swap in “sacramental eating”; the Reformed allow some sacramental eating can fall on the unworthy — so Strimesius prelibates that term before settling who the unworthy are, or whether the attribution is true and necessary.
source_text: ANNOTATIO VI. De Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali Indignorum. §. I. Manducationis corporis Christi Oralis terminum & rationem, etsi plenius, Annotatione præcedente, excussimus; tamen, cùm ex una parte, Lutheranorum emunctoris judicii Theologi, ad terminum hunc, de Indignis quoque prædicandum, prædicatumque, nauseare incipiant, Sacramentalis Manducationis termino in istius locum surrogatô; ex altera parte Reformati quandam corporis Christi Sacramentalem Manducationem, etiam in indignos cadere posse haud abnuant; de hoc Sacramentalis Manducationis termino aliquid hôc locô prælibandum fuerit, antequam vel de Indignis, quibus ista Manducatio tribuitur, vel de Attributionis hujus Veritate & Necessitate, quicquam determinemus.
